## Why
- **Several syncs of one bank at once.** Opening the app, Sync now, the hourly job and a new consent could all start a sync of the same bank together. The open route's "already running" check happened before the sync was marked as running, and its memory of recent tries was lost on restart.
- **One account blocked the others.** A rate limit on one account dropped every remaining account of that connection, and the connection-wide 20-hour wait then held all of them back.
- **A failed first sync could lose history.** Banks share full history only shortly after consent. If the first sync failed, nothing retried it soon enough.
- **Any 401 counted as ended consent.** A wrong App ID, a bad private key or clock skew also return 401, so connections were wrongly flipped to "reconnect".

## What changes
- **A lease per connection.** It is taken with `claim_bank_sync` (15 minutes, extended by `hold_bank_sync`).
  - All four triggers go through one helper. A trigger that can't get the lease reports "already syncing" (409 for Sync now).
  - A run whose lease ran out can't advance the date window, record balances or publish a result.
- **Timing per account** (`next_allowed_at`, `last_attempted_at`, `last_error` on each account).
  - Accounts are fetched independently.
  - The bank's Retry-After is honoured, capped at 24 hours.
  - Background runs keep 20 hours between fetches of the same account. Syncs with the owner present stay hourly.
  - The connection's error lists each account's problem.
- **First sync retries.** A first sync that fails for a passing reason (network, timeout, 429, 5xx) gets up to 3 durable retries, at least 20 minutes apart.
  - The connection message then says the account's history hasn't been fetched yet, and Home says so too.
- **401s are classified by error code.** For a 401 with an unknown code, Moneo asks Enable Banking about the app itself:
  - If the App ID or key is rejected, it says so, does **not** mark the consent ended, and holds the accounts for 6 hours. Saving a new key clears that wait.
  - If the app check passes, the consent is marked ended.
- Migration `202611130003_bank_sync_leases.sql`, SQL regression `supabase/tests/bank-sync-lease.sql`, and two README sentences on first-sync retries and per-account limits.

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One account rate limited, the others still land | fail: account B not landed | pass |
| Unexplained 401: ask about the app before ending consent | fail: connection marked expired | pass |
| A run whose lease ran out doesn't move the cursor or publish | fail: cursor advanced | pass |
| A first sync that failed for a passing reason is retried, at most 3 times | fail: 0 retries | pass |
| Open route leaves a bank another trigger is syncing alone | fail: second sync started | pass |
| Cron starts a background sync per connection with an account due | fail: connection-wide 20h query | pass |

Stacked on #209 (`t3/bank-raw-data`). This is part 5 of the bank sync and organizer redesign.

## What changes

Fixed rules now run before any AI when rows land. They use the bank's own data that #209 stores in the `bank_transaction_raw` sidecar.

- **Own transfers**
  - Proof now includes:
    - the counterparty IBAN from the bank's data;
    - the bank's account ids;
    - an IBAN in the CSV row (the only proof before).
  - A top-up to one of the owner's IBANs is marked `kind='transfer'` even when the other side is missing.
  - Equal amounts in two of the owner's accounts with no proof become a single card. No card is raised when there is a third matching leg, or when either row names someone else's IBAN.
  - When two legs are equally close, the row is left for the owner. Before, the lower id was paired silently.

The old categorizer is replaced. It looked only at the description and left uncertain rows out, so about 46% of real rows stayed blank. The new organizer runs as the first wave of the agent team; the wave order is unchanged.

1. **Labels without the AI, in this order:**
   - the owner's rule;
   - confirmed merchant memory;
   - the bank's merchant category code or fee posting, matched to Moneo's default categories;
   - consistent owner history.
2. **The AI gets the rest, one item per identity.** Each item carries masked row context: description, amount, date, the bank's counterparty and codes from the raw sidecar, and the identity.
   - Three read tools: the identity's owner-labelled history, related rows, and owner examples per category.
   - It must answer every item with category, merchant, confidence and reason, or with a question. Each answer is checked with Zod.
   - Missing or unusable answers are asked once more, then become questions.
   - It may create up to 5 new categories per run, marked `created_by='ai'`.
3. **Applying:**
   - High labels, and medium ones while calibration holds, go through `apply_ai_organization`. They are marked AI and can be undone.
   - Rules, memory and bank-code labels carry their own source (`rule`, `memory`, `system`; migration `202611130007`). Memory rows are never overwritten, and owner rows are never touched.
   - Low labels become one question per identity in `organize_questions`.
   - No owner rules or owner corrections are written.
4. **Batching:**
   - Batches hold about 6,000 tokens or 40 items.
   - Parallelism starts at 2, grows to at most 6, and halves on a 429 with a growing pause.
   - A ChatGPT usage-limit error ends the AI work cleanly, without failing the run.
   - Decisions are cached per identity, so repeated identities cost one decision.
5. **Privacy:** no IBANs are sent (only a "to own account" flag). Account numbers are masked, and private people are sent without their name.
6. **Calibration kill switch:** if fewer than 90% of the last 200 judged AI labels were right (with at least 50 judged), medium labels stop being auto-applied and the reason is logged. A label counts as right when it was kept for 14 days or confirmed, and wrong when it was undone or changed.

Stacked on #216 (`t3/ai-organizer`). This is part 7 of the bank sync and organizer redesign.

## What changes

Each workspace now gets one organize and analysis pass, instead of one agent run per import or per bank sync.

- **Debounce.**
  - When an import or a sync asks for a pass, the run waits 3 minutes, then keeps waiting while any bank sync of the workspace still holds its lease (30 minutes at most). Everything that lands in that time joins the same run.
  - A request that arrives while a run is working triggers exactly one follow-up run after it.
  - Manual and backlog starts still begin immediately.
- **Analysis only on changed data.** After organizing, the recurring, anomaly, budget, forecaster and writer waves run only when the transactions changed since the last completed analysis. This is checked by a data fingerprint: row count, the sum of row versions and the latest insert, from migration `202611130008`. Manual runs always analyse.
- **Leftovers.** A run records when to retry the rows it left blank:
  - when the plan limit resets, if the provider says so;
  - right away when the run's budget was spent;
  - otherwise in an hour.

  The hourly backlog check retries at that time. Rows the AI actually failed on are not retried in a loop.
- **Daily sync.** Once one account of a workspace is due, its other banks join it if their last try was at least 12 hours ago. On that day this costs one extra fetch, which stays within PSD2's ~4 a day.
- **First review.** It starts once every bank's history has arrived, or 24 hours after the first rows, whichever comes first. It no longer fires from the first bank's rows alone.
- **Budget check.** It still runs only when the owner has spending limits.

### Connect your bank (optional)

Moneo syncs booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). It is free for personal use. Each sync is an ordinary import that you can review and undo. Moneo also keeps what the bank sent for each transaction (codes, counterparty details, references) on your computer to help organize it; undoing a sync removes it.

1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create an application in the **Production** environment.
2. Fill in the application form:
   - Redirect URL: `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback`
   - Privacy policy URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/privacy.html`
   - Terms of service URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/terms.html`
3. Let the control panel make the key pair, and keep the downloaded private key file (`<application-id>.pem`).
4. In the control panel, link your own bank accounts to the application. Only linked accounts can be synced.
5. In Moneo, go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks** (also on the Import page). Paste the application ID, paste the private key or upload the `.pem` file, and click **Save and check**.
6. Click **Choose a bank**, pick yours, click **Connect bank** and approve access at your bank.
